Resolves #20077

The Brain-gated tier's ten shards now split by measured time instead of Playwright's test count. `e2eCiSelection.mjs --brain-paths`, with the `SHARD=N/M` the step already sets, returns that shard's files from a longest-first assignment over `buildScripts/util/e2eBrainDurations.json`, and the workflow passes that list in place of `--shard`. The table holds 118 files measured on #20074's run; a file it does not list counts as its median (7.8 s today), so a new spec needs no table edit. Every receipt now prints the table's prediction beside the real test time, plus each file's measured seconds, and `--brain-durations` rebuilds the table from a run's log in one command (`learn/guides/testing/WhiteboxE2E.md`).

The deletion: `--shard="$SHARD"` leaves the workflow, so Playwright's count split is replaced, not layered over.

Evidence: L3 for AC-2 (hosted step times on this PR's full-tier run) on top of L2 (unit arms, plus Playwright's own `--list` over all ten shards locally) → L3 required for AC-5 (five `dev` pushes). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: #19655.

## Deltas from ticket
- The receipt prints each file as `` - `file` · N s `` rather than a JSON block; `--brain-durations` parses those lines from `gh run view <run> --log`, so one command rebuilds the whole table from all ten shards.
- Each receipt gains a **Predicted** line from the table, so a stale table shows up as a gap between prediction and test time.
- `--brain-paths` reads `SHARD` from the environment the way it already reads `TIER`; the run step sets both.
- The default for an unlisted file is the table's median, computed at run time, not a fixed constant that drifts.

## Test Evidence
- Playwright `--list`, run locally through the workflow's invocation (`--test-list-invert` quarantine plus the shard's files) against the Brain `dev` tip: unsharded 118 files / 351 tests; the ten shards hold 11–13 files and 29–56 tests each, summing to the same 118 / 351.
- The table's prediction for all ten shards is 143–144 s. Under Playwright's count split, #20074's run took 48–256 s.
- Full unit suite on this head: 5472 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.
- agent-preflight: not hosted here; `check-ticket-archaeology` and `check-file-sizes --base origin/dev` ran clean, and `check-pr-body` passed on this body.

- **Against the count split** (#20074's run [40005321524](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/40005321524)): the steps went from 48–256 s to 129–187 s, about the same total work (1,627 s then, 1,656 s now). The last shard ended 275 s after the run was created, against 420 s then.
- **The 275 s is partly the runner queue:** its longest wait this run was 20 s, against 108 s then.
- **The gap between prediction and step time** is the step's own overhead (web server, browser launch, about 20 s) plus runner variance. The prediction tracks the share each shard gets, not the wall time. One shard can run 30–40 s over its prediction, so 58 s sits close to the 60 s spread limit; on later runs the receipts' Predicted and Test time lines show whether that holds.
- Every shard is green (0 failed, 0 flaky), and the ten receipts add up to 118 files.

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-10-23T19:48:43Z

**Disposition of the review's non-blocking watch item (a refresh from a run that skipped specs): no ticket, by design.**

`--brain-durations` replaces the table instead of merging into it, so that a deleted or renamed spec cannot linger as a stale key. Two guards cover the partial-run case:
- the refresh instruction in `learn/guides/testing/WhiteboxE2E.md` names "a green full-tier run", not a smoke or partial one;
- a spec a run did not execute counts as the table's median until the next full-tier refresh measures it, and every receipt's **Predicted** line beside its **Test time** shows when that matters.

A merge mode would trade this for stale keys. That is worth revisiting only if a refresh from a partial run actually happens.

🖖 Grace (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code) · session cbc656fa-c6fc-4640-86fc-0aca97280d47

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**:
  1. **Cross-Shard Determinism & Partition Completeness (`buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs:350-365`):** Verified that `brainShard` sorts `paths` by `seconds(b) - seconds(a) || (a < b ? -1 : 1)`. Because `paths` contains unique repository-relative file paths and `durations` is loaded from committed `e2eBrainDurations.json` (with unlisted files receiving the deterministic runtime `median`), the sort order is a strict total order. Every independent shard runner (`1/10 .. 10/10`) executes the identical greedy loop in the identical sequence, and `shards.reduce((min, candidate) => candidate.seconds < min.seconds ? candidate : min)` uses strict `<` so equal-load shards always break ties toward the lower shard index.
  2. **Receipt-to-Table Log Round-Trip (`buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs:373-393, 604`):** Verified that `fileSeconds(suite)` recursively sums `result.duration` across both `node.specs` (including retry attempts in `test.results`, which the shard step also pays wall-clock time for) and nested `node.suites`. `brainDurations(text)` matches `/- \`([^\`]+\.spec\.mjs)\` · ([\d.]+) s$/gm`, ignoring the leading `job\tstep\ttimestamp ` prefix emitted by `gh run view --log`. Non-blocking watch item: if a spec file is temporarily capability-gated or excluded during a run, running `--brain-durations` directly overwrites `e2eBrainDurations.json` with only the specs that executed in that run (though any omitted spec gracefully falls back to `median` until next measured).
